title: Ensure default password of root is not allowed
description: To assist users in changing default password for "root" account
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1 Ensure default password of root is not allowed

audit.command: From a management host try to log in to the BIG-IP as root (SSH and console) with the factory default password 'default'. The login must be rejected. Also confirm root access is restricted (System > Platform).

remediation.command:
- Log in to the Configuration utility.
- For System, select Platform.
- Under User Administration, choose the Password box for either Root Account or Admin Account.
- Enter the new password.
- Enter the same password in the Confirm box for the account that you chose in step 3.
- Select Update.
- If you have updated the password for Admin Account, the system logs you out of the Configuration utility, and you must log in again using the new password.

title: Ensure default password of admin is not used
description: To assist users in changing default password for 'admin' account
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.2 Ensure default password of admin is not used

audit.command: From a management host try to log in to the Configuration utility and SSH as admin with the factory default password 'admin'. The login must be rejected.

remediation.command:
- Log in to the Configuration utility.
- For System, select Platform.
- Under User Administration, choose the Password box for either Root Account or Admin Account.
- Enter the new password.
- Enter the same password in the Confirm box for the account that you chose in step 3.
- Select Update.
- If you have updated the password for Admin Account, the system logs you out of the Configuration utility, and you must log in again using the new password.

title: Configure Secure Password Policy
description: To assist users in maintaining strong passwords, ensure that passwords are changed at appropriate intervals and new passwords to be used PASS requires every CIS minimum in auth password-policy (tmsh lists properties alphabetically): expiration-warning >= 14, lockout-duration >= 300, max-duration <= 180, max-login-failures 1-3, min-duration >= 90, minimum-length >= 12, password-memory >= 24, policy-enforcement enabled and at least one required lowercase, numeric, special and uppercase character. Audited against tmsh output with defaults shown: save the concatenated output of 'tmsh list auth password-policy all-properties', 'tmsh list auth source all-properties', 'tmsh list auth remote-user all-properties', 'tmsh list auth radius all-properties', 'tmsh list sys httpd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list cli global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list sys ntp', 'tmsh list sys snmp all-properties', 'tmsh list sys syslog' and 'tmsh list net self all-properties'. Patterns are scoped to the named top-level block.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.3 Configure Secure Password Policy

remediation.command:
tmsh modify auth password-policy policy-enforcement enabled minimum-length 12 required-lowercase 1 required-uppercase 1 required-numeric 1 required-special 1 max-duration 180 min-duration 90 expiration-warning 14 password-memory 24 max-login-failures 3 lockout-duration 300
tmsh save sys config
# CIS guidance:
Configuring the password policy using the Configuration utility
1. Log in to the Configuration utility.
2.
Navigate to System > Users > Authentication.
3. Under Password Policy, locate the Secure Password Enforcement setting and set it to meet below minimum requirements :
Configuring the password policy using tmsh
1. Log in to tmsh by typing the following command:
tmsh:
modify /auth password-policy
The minimum requirements :
- Secure Password Enforcement : Enabled
- Minimum Password Length is 12
- Required Lowercase is 1
- Required Uppercase is 1
- Required Numeric is 1
- Required Special Characters is 1
- Maximum Duration (in Days): 180
- Minimum Duration (in Days): 90
- Expiration Warning ( in days):14
- EnsurePassword Memory is 24
- Ensure Maximum Login Failures is 3
- User Lockout :  Automatically enable locked-out users after : 300 seconds others are done through tmsh only.**

title: Ensure that Remote Radius is used for Authentication Only
description: To specify the authentication mechanism that F5 systems use for external (remote) users PASS requires the system-auth RADIUS configuration to use service-type authenticate-only. Audited against tmsh output with defaults shown: save the concatenated output of 'tmsh list auth password-policy all-properties', 'tmsh list auth source all-properties', 'tmsh list auth remote-user all-properties', 'tmsh list auth radius all-properties', 'tmsh list sys httpd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list cli global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list sys ntp', 'tmsh list sys snmp all-properties', 'tmsh list sys syslog' and 'tmsh list net self all-properties'. Patterns are scoped to the named top-level block.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure that Remote Radius is used for Authentication Only

remediation.command:
tmsh modify auth radius system-auth service-type authenticate-only
tmsh save sys config
# CIS guidance:
1-Log in to the Configuration utility using the administrator account.
2-Navigate to System > Users > Authentication.
3-In the Authentication section, click Change.
4-Select Remote - RADIUS from the User Directory drop-down menu.
5-Define the RADIUS server configuration settings, including the port and shared secret settings:
6- For "Service Type": select "Authentication Only"
7-Click Finished.

title: Ensure redundant remote authentication servers are configured
description: Having multiple points of authentication is important in the event that the primary remote authentication source goes down. PASS requires the system-auth RADIUS configuration to reference at least two servers (primary and secondary). Audited against tmsh output with defaults shown: save the concatenated output of 'tmsh list auth password-policy all-properties', 'tmsh list auth source all-properties', 'tmsh list auth remote-user all-properties', 'tmsh list auth radius all-properties', 'tmsh list sys httpd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list cli global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list sys ntp', 'tmsh list sys snmp all-properties', 'tmsh list sys syslog' and 'tmsh list net self all-properties'. Patterns are scoped to the named top-level block.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure redundant remote authentication servers are configured

remediation.command:
tmsh create auth radius-server system_auth_name2 server 10.0.0.12 secret <secret>
tmsh modify auth radius system-auth servers replace-all-with { system_auth_name1 system_auth_name2 }
tmsh save sys config
# CIS guidance:
1-Log in to the Configuration utility using the administrator account.
2-Navigate to System > Users > Authentication.
3-In the Authentication section, click Change.
4-Select Remote - RADIUS from the User Directory drop-down menu.
5-Define the RADIUS server configuration settings, including the port and shared secret settings:
6-For "Service Type": select "Authentication Only"
7-This should be completed for Primary RADIUS server as well as for Secondary RADIUS server.
8-Click Finished.

title: Ensure minimum SSH Encryption algorithm is set to aes128-cbc
description: To set strong SSH Encryption algorithm.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure minimum SSH Encryption algorithm is set to aes128-cbc

audit.command: Run 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties' and review the include statement: a 'Ciphers' line must restrict SSH to the organisation-approved ciphers (the CIS example starts the list with aes128-cbc, aes128-ctr, aes192-ctr, aes256-ctr). Note the CIS example also lists arcfour ciphers, which are weak; prefer CTR/GCM ciphers only.

remediation.command:
1-Log in to tmsh by typing the following command:tmsh
2-To modify the sshd configuration, type the following command to start the vi editor:edit /sys sshd all-properties
3-To change the list of ciphers, you can navigate to the line that starts with the include statement, and use the keyword Ciphers :
include "Ciphers aes128-cbc,aes128-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes256-
ctr,arcfour128,arcfour256,arcfour"

reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure redundant NTP servers are configured appropriately

# CIS guidance:

title: Ensure port lockdown for self IP is set
description: to secure the BIG-IP system from unwanted connection attempts on self-IP. FAILs if any self IP has allow-service all or default (Port Lockdown must be Allow None or Allow Custom). Audited against tmsh output with defaults shown: save the concatenated output of 'tmsh list auth password-policy all-properties', 'tmsh list auth source all-properties', 'tmsh list auth remote-user all-properties', 'tmsh list auth radius all-properties', 'tmsh list sys httpd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list cli global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list sys ntp', 'tmsh list sys snmp all-properties', 'tmsh list sys syslog' and 'tmsh list net self all-properties'. Patterns are scoped to the named top-level block.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure port lockdown for self IP is set

remediation.command:
tmsh modify net self <self-ip> allow-service none
(or) tmsh modify net self <self-ip> allow-service replace-all-with { tcp:443 }
tmsh save sys config
# CIS guidance:
1-Log in to the Configuration utility.
2-Go to Network > Self IPs.
3-Select the relevant self IP address.
4-If the specified interface does not need to listen to incoming connections ( Example BGP ,BDF ..etc) , set "Port Lockdown" to "Allow None"
5-If the specified interface need to listen for incoming connections , set "Port Lockdown" to "Allow Custom". Then in the "Custom List" add needed ports only.

title: Ensure minimum SNMP version is set to V3 for agent access
description: To disable the usage of weak SNMP protocols FAILs if any SNMP v1/v2c community (community-name) is configured under sys snmp; define SNMPv3 users instead. Audited against tmsh output with defaults shown: save the concatenated output of 'tmsh list auth password-policy all-properties', 'tmsh list auth source all-properties', 'tmsh list auth remote-user all-properties', 'tmsh list auth radius all-properties', 'tmsh list sys httpd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list cli global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list sys ntp', 'tmsh list sys snmp all-properties', 'tmsh list sys syslog' and 'tmsh list net self all-properties'. Patterns are scoped to the named top-level block.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure minimum SNMP version is set to V3 for agent access

remediation.command:
tmsh modify sys snmp communities delete { <community> }
tmsh modify sys snmp users add { v3user { username v3user auth-protocol sha auth-password <pw> privacy-protocol aes privacy-password <pw> security-level auth-privacy } }
tmsh save sys config

1-Login to Configuration utility
2- Go to System > SNMP > Agent > SNMP Access (v1, v2c) :
Select all listed entries and click "Delete"
3-Go to System > SNMP > Agent > SNMP Access (v3) :
Make sure there is one entry at least , otherwise create one.

title: Ensure that Remote Syslog Servers are configured
description: To ensure that logs are sent to external servers PASS requires at least one remote syslog server (sys syslog remote-servers ... host). Audited against tmsh output with defaults shown: save the concatenated output of 'tmsh list auth password-policy all-properties', 'tmsh list auth source all-properties', 'tmsh list auth remote-user all-properties', 'tmsh list auth radius all-properties', 'tmsh list sys httpd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys sshd all-properties', 'tmsh list sys global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list cli global-settings all-properties', 'tmsh list sys ntp', 'tmsh list sys snmp all-properties', 'tmsh list sys syslog' and 'tmsh list net self all-properties'. Patterns are scoped to the named top-level block.
reference: CIS F5 Networks Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5 Ensure that Remote Syslog Servers are configured

remediation.command:
tmsh modify sys syslog remote-servers add { remotesyslog1 { host 10.0.0.50 remote-port 514 } }
tmsh save sys config
# CIS guidance:
1-Log in to the Configuration utility.
2-Go to System > Logs > Configuration > Remote Logging.
3-For Remote IP, enter the destination syslog server IP address, or FQDN. (DNS server configuration required)
4-For Remote Port, enter the remote syslog server UDP port (default is 514).
5-Select Add.
6-Select Update.

title: Ensure Prelogin 'Login Banner' is set
description: PASS requires sys sshd banner enabled (set banner-text to the approved notice). remediation.command:

tmsh save sys config
# CIS guidance:
1-Log in to the Configuration utility.
